title: Why are people heading to cinemas in cat ears? It's CatVideoFest
answer: They're going to CatVideoFest, a feature-length compilation of funny and sweet cat videos that tours movie theaters every year. Fans treat it like a party and dress the part in cat ears, cat T-shirts and even cat masks, and screenings usually support local cat rescues.
body:
CatVideoFest is exactly what it sounds like: roughly 75 minutes of cat clips, short animations and internet favorites, stitched together with no narration and shown on a big screen. Curator Will Braden, known for the deadpan "Henri, le Chat Noir" videos, sifts through thousands of submissions a year and loosely groups the picks into themes. The 2026 edition is playing at chains such as AMC and at independent and museum cinemas across the U.S., and it also screens in the U.K., Australia, New Zealand and parts of Europe and Asia.

The costumes are part of the fun rather than a rule. Audiences come in cat ears and feline prints, cheer for favorite clips and laugh out loud, which makes the screening feel closer to a sing-along than a quiet movie night. Afternoon shows skew toward families; evening shows draw groups of friends. Someone heading out might text, "Ears on, we're seeing 75 minutes of cats tonight."

The festival grew out of the Internet Cat Video Festival that Minneapolis's Walker Art Center began in 2012. Braden started CatVideoFest as its own touring program in 2016 and began bringing it to U.S. theaters in 2019; it reached U.K. cinemas about two years ago. Theaters are encouraged to partner with a local cat charity, and many donate part of ticket sales or invite rescue groups to the show.

It is trending now because the fall 2026 tour has hit more screens, and a BBC report on Nov. 21 about costumed crowds at a Newcastle screening got people asking what the fuss was about. It is family-friendly, so it is an easy outing to suggest for kids who already watch cat videos on their phones.
in_the_news: CatVideoFest 2026 is touring theaters this fall, and a BBC story on Nov. 21, 2026, about fans in cat ears sent the question to Google.

faq.a: An annual, roughly 75-minute compilation of cat videos and animations curated by Will Braden and shown in movie theaters, with part of the proceeds often going to local cat charities.

faq.q: Do you have to wear cat ears to CatVideoFest?
faq.a: No. Costumes are optional; many fans just enjoy dressing up for it.
Yes. It is made as a family-friendly program and many theaters schedule daytime showings for families.
Check your local cinema or the AMC listing; the tour runs at different theaters on different dates through the fall.
